correctness.rationale: Positive definiteness is certified by principal minors 3, 2, 23/4. For every t>=0, the unconstrained first coordinate equals q/D with q=(t-1/2)(t-1), and the other two are strictly positive via positive-coefficient D±q. When q<=0 the x1=0 solution has nonnegative reduced gradient -q/((t+1)(t+4)); otherwise full unconstrained solution is feasible, so strict convex KKT gives global uniqueness. In two dimensions the x1=0 iff c max(b2,0)/(d+t)-b1>=0 test is monotone, proving the minimal dimension. Eigenvalue ratio declines strictly; strict KKT witness signs at three t values imply robust reentry. verify_ridge.py independently checks exact identities and nine sample active sets; the analytical proof, not sampling, establishes infinite range.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2026 paper analyzes fixed-parameter active-set solvers and improving ridge conditioning, not monotonicity of optimal supports across regularization. The 2002 and 2004 nonnegative Tikhonov papers analyze methods to solve regularized problems rather than the sharp dimension-two monotonicity theorem and explicit three-dimensional support reentry at exact thresholds. Closest identified mathematical-record findings concern different quantities, and lasso path results concern the L1 penalty. An unindexed equivalent example remains possible.

value.rationale: Parametric active-set warm starts often assume nesting or use cheap support continuation during regularization. A minimal n=3 robust counterexample with positive forcing and strictly improving conditioning shows no such guarantee follows from ridge regularization or SPD structure. The universal n<=2 theorem makes the boundary precise, the explicit rational thresholds make it reproducible, and the robustness check shows it is not a numerical coincidence. No all-dimensional claim is made.
